title: Degree adverbs (B1)
note: Two jobs: 0–100 scale (a bit / quite / very / really / extremely) and need (too / enough / far too). Czech ne moc = not very. Not so/such, not extreme adjectives. Bank 12 = one pass. Seeded from Martina's `not so much relaxing` 2026-08-16. Rebuilt 2026-08-28 after smoke: unit had been a coursebook lump. THICKENED 2026-09-04 by the B1 agent loop: 12 -> 27 items. The 12 were one pass over the scale with one item per word; the scale words now get three or four each, the too/enough pair gets six, and both take an adverb as well as an adjective (extremely well, quite slowly, well enough). C17 - the Remember recap card is cut. Intro merged 9 cards -> 6 (a bit + quite on one card, very + really + extremely on one), because cards 1-4 each restated one row of card 0's table. C4 - the Common errors bullet bolded `not so much`, which reads as a model sentence; it is a strike now (C32). A4 - the six article demands carry the Czech demonstrative that licenses `the` (Ta voda, To pocasi, Ten vylet, To more, Ty listky) or lost the article (after a long walk). F4/F3 - `It's` and `She's` are read by the lint as possessives of unknown names; the uncontracted form is in `en` and the contraction stays in `accepts`. SECOND PASS the same day, by the parallel run of the same loop: the 27-item version above drilled the six words the pack already had. B1-PLAN asks this unit to ALSO absorb so / such and the degree cluster parked in codex/parked-a2-adverb-clusters.json, so that is folded in here - a little, slightly, fairly, rather, hardly, completely, totally, perfectly, almost, nearly, particularly, plus so and such. 12 -> 39 items. Four of the 27 were dropped as repeats of a frame already covered (a third `quite`, a second `not very`, a third `too + for me`). `increasingly` was NOT folded in: it is a B2 register word and would be the only item here a B1 student could not produce; it stays parked. The intro went 6 -> 9 cards because the new words need naming (C11): low / middle / high-and-top / all-the-way (completely + totally + perfectly, where *very right* is the error) / not-quite (almost + nearly + hardly, with the no-second-negative rule) / too and enough / so and such / errors. The adverb items from the first pass (extremely well, quite slowly, well enough) are named on cards 0 and 6.

cards.title: How strong? The 0–100 scale
points: These words say how strong an adjective is.
They go in front of an adverb too: **quite** slowly.

cards.title: Low: a bit · a little · slightly
cards.title_cz: Nízko: a bit · a little · slightly
points: All three say *only a small amount*.
**slightly** is the one you use with a comparative.

cards.title: Middle: fairly · quite · rather
points: **rather** often carries a hint of surprise.

cards.title: High and top: very · really · extremely
cards.title_cz: Vysoko a nahoře: very · really · extremely
points: **extremely** is the top. Nothing sits above it.

cards.title: All the way: completely · totally · perfectly
points: Some adjectives are all or nothing: right, wrong, full.
Those take these words, not the 0–100 ones.

cards.title: Not quite: almost · nearly · hardly
points: **hardly** means *almost not*, so no second negative.

cards.title: too and enough
points: These two are not on the scale — they compare with a **need**.
**enough** goes after an adjective or adverb, but before a noun.

cards.title: so and such
points: **so** goes with an adjective on its own.
**such** goes with a noun, and takes **a** in the singular.

rows: It was **so** cold that we went home.

cards.title: Common errors
points: Czech *ne moc* + adjective is **not very**, never ~~not so much~~.

items.en: It is a bit cold.
items.explanation: a bit = low on the scale.
items.explanation_cz: a bit = nízko na stupnici.

items.en: We were quite tired after a long walk.
items.cz: Byli jsme po dlouhé procházce docela unavení.
items.gap: We were ____ tired after a long walk. (middle)
accepts: We were quite tired after a long walk.
items.explanation: quite = middle of the scale.
items.explanation_cz: quite = uprostřed stupnice.

items.en: The exam was very hard.
items.explanation: very = high on the scale. really sits here too.
items.explanation_cz: very = vysoko na stupnici. really sem patří taky.

items.en: The water is warm enough to swim in.
items.cz: Ta voda je dost teplá na koupání.
items.gap: The water is warm ____ to swim in.
accepts: The water is warm enough to swim in.
The water is warm enough to swim.
items.wrong: The water is enough warm to swim in.
items.explanation: enough after the adjective, then to: warm enough to swim in.
items.explanation_cz: enough za přídavným jménem, pak to: warm enough to swim in.

items.en: The weather was extremely difficult for driving.
items.cz: To počasí bylo na řízení extrémně náročné.
items.gap: The weather was ____ difficult for driving. (top)
accepts: The weather was extremely difficult for driving.
items.explanation: extremely = the top of the 0–100 scale.
items.explanation_cz: extremely = vrchol stupnice 0–100.

items.en: The trip was not very relaxing.
accepts: The trip was not very relaxing.
The trip was not really relaxing.
items.wrong: The trip was not so much relaxing.
items.explanation: Czech *ne moc* = not very. Never *not so much relaxing*.
items.explanation_cz: České *ne moc* = not very. Nikdy *not so much relaxing*.

items.en: The sea was too cold to swim in.
items.cz: To moře bylo příliš studené na koupání.
items.gap: The sea was ____ cold to swim in.
accepts: The sea was too cold to swim in.
items.wrong: The sea was very cold to swim in.
items.explanation: too = past the need. *very cold* only describes.
items.explanation_cz: too = za potřebou. *very cold* jen popisuje.

items.en: He drove too fast to stop.
items.cz: Jel příliš rychle na to, aby zastavil.
accepts: He drove too fast to stop.
items.wrong: He drove very fast to stop.
items.explanation: too + adverb + to: too fast to stop.
items.explanation_cz: too + příslovce + to: too fast to stop.

items.en: Our room was not big enough for four people.
items.cz: Náš pokoj nebyl dost velký pro čtyři lidi.
items.gap: Our room was not big ____ for four people.
accepts: Our room was not big enough for four people.
Our room was not big enough for 4 people.
items.wrong: Our room was not enough big for four people.
items.explanation: enough comes AFTER the adjective: big enough.
items.explanation_cz: enough stojí AŽ ZA přídavným jménem: big enough.

items.en: She is old enough to drive.
items.cz: Je dost stará na to, aby řídila.
accepts: She is old enough to drive.
items.wrong: She is enough old to drive.
items.explanation: enough after the adjective, then to: old enough to drive.
items.explanation_cz: enough za přídavným jménem, pak to: old enough to drive.

items.en: The tickets were far too expensive.
items.cz: Ty lístky byly až příliš drahé.
accepts: The tickets were far too expensive.
The tickets were way too expensive.
items.wrong: The tickets were very too expensive.
items.explanation: To strengthen too, use far/way. *very too* is impossible.
items.explanation_cz: Pro zesílení too: far/way. *very too* nejde.

items.en: We arrived a bit late.
items.explanation: a bit = low on the scale, with adverbs too.
items.explanation_cz: a bit = nízko na stupnici, i u příslovcí.

items.en: Honza was extremely tired after work.
items.cz: Honza byl po práci extrémně unavený.
accepts: Honza was extremely tired after work.
items.explanation: **extremely** is the top of the scale — above *very*, which is only high.
items.explanation_cz: **extremely** je vrchol stupnice — nad *very*, které je jen vysoko.

items.en: This flat is a bit small for us.
items.cz: Tenhle byt je pro nás trochu malý.
items.gap: This flat is ____ small for us. (low)
accepts: This flat is a bit small for us.
This flat is a little small for us.
items.explanation: *trochu* is the bottom of the scale: **a bit** small. *a little* is the same height.
items.explanation_cz: *trochu* je spodek stupnice: **a bit** small. *a little* je stejně vysoko.

items.en: The meeting was really useful.
items.explanation: **really** and **very** are the same height, so either is right here.
items.explanation_cz: **really** a **very** jsou stejně vysoko, takže tady je správně obojí.

items.en: Klara speaks English extremely well.
items.explanation: These words work in front of an adverb too: **extremely** well.
items.explanation_cz: Tahle slova fungují i před příslovcem: **extremely** well.

items.en: We walked quite slowly.
items.explanation: **quite** in front of an adverb: quite slowly, quite late, quite well.
items.explanation_cz: **quite** před příslovcem: quite slowly, quite late, quite well.

items.en: The hotel was not very clean.
accepts: The hotel was not very clean.
The hotel was not really clean.
items.wrong: The hotel was not so much clean.
items.explanation: Czech *ne moc* is **not very**. *Not so much* in front of an adjective is not English.
items.explanation_cz: České *ne moc* je **not very**. *Not so much* před přídavným jménem není angličtina.

items.en: The box was too heavy to lift.
items.cz: Ta krabice byla příliš těžká na zvednutí.
items.gap: The box was ____ heavy to lift.
accepts: The box was too heavy to lift.
items.wrong: The box was very heavy to lift.
items.explanation: **too** heavy to lift means it did not get lifted. *Very heavy* would only describe it.
items.explanation_cz: **too** heavy to lift znamená, že se nezvedla. *Very heavy* by ji jen popsalo.

items.en: It was too late to call her.
items.cz: Bylo příliš pozdě na to jí volat.
items.gap: It was ____ late to call her.
accepts: It was too late to call her.
items.wrong: It was very late to call her.
items.explanation: **too** late to call = the call did not happen. That is the *to* that follows **too**.
items.explanation_cz: **too** late to call = k hovoru nedošlo. To je to *to*, které jde po **too**.

items.en: Is your coffee hot enough?
items.wrong: Is your coffee enough hot?
items.explanation: **enough** goes after the adjective, in a question as well: hot **enough**.
items.explanation_cz: **enough** jde za přídavné jméno, i v otázce: hot **enough**.

items.en: Eva doesn't speak English well enough.
accepts: Eva doesn't speak English well enough.
Eva does not speak English well enough.
items.wrong: Eva doesn't speak English enough well.
items.explanation: **enough** follows an adverb the same way it follows an adjective: well **enough**.
items.explanation_cz: **enough** jde za příslovce stejně jako za přídavné jméno: well **enough**.

items.en: The traffic was far too heavy this morning.
items.cz: Ten provoz byl dnes ráno až příliš hustý.
items.gap: The traffic was ____ too heavy this morning.
accepts: The traffic was far too heavy this morning.
The traffic was way too heavy this morning.
items.wrong: The traffic was very too heavy this morning.
items.explanation: To strengthen **too**, use **far** or **way**. *Very too* is impossible.
items.explanation_cz: Pro zesílení **too** se používá **far** nebo **way**. *Very too* nejde.

items.en: I am a little tired.
items.wrong: I am little tired.
items.explanation: **a little** is the same height as *a bit*, and it keeps its **a**.
items.explanation_cz: **a little** je stejně vysoko jako *a bit* a nechává si své **a**.

items.en: The second one is slightly bigger.
items.cz: Ten druhý je o něco větší.
accepts: The second one is slightly bigger.
items.wrong: The second one is slightly much bigger.
items.explanation: **slightly** is the small-difference word, and it works in front of a comparative.
items.explanation_cz: **slightly** je slovo pro malý rozdíl a funguje před druhým stupněm.

items.en: The exam was fairly easy.
items.wrong: The exam was fairly much easy.
items.explanation: **fairly** sits in the middle, close to *quite*.
items.explanation_cz: **fairly** je uprostřed, blízko k *quite*.

items.en: It was rather cold for June.
accepts: It was rather cold for June.
items.wrong: It was rather much cold for June.
items.explanation: **rather** is middle too, and it often carries a hint of surprise.
items.explanation_cz: **rather** je taky uprostřed a často v sobě nese náznak překvapení.

items.en: I hardly know him.
items.wrong: I hardly not know him.
items.explanation: **hardly** already means *almost not*, so there is no second negative.
items.explanation_cz: **hardly** už samo znamená *skoro ne*, takže tam není druhý zápor.

items.en: You are completely right.
items.wrong: You are very right.
items.explanation: *right* is all or nothing, so it takes **completely**, not a 0–100 word.
items.explanation_cz: *right* je všechno, nebo nic, takže má **completely**, ne slovo ze škály 0–100.

items.en: That is totally wrong.
items.wrong: That is very wrong.
items.explanation: **totally** is the twin of *completely*, and *wrong* is another all-or-nothing word.
items.explanation_cz: **totally** je dvojče k *completely* a *wrong* je další slovo typu všechno, nebo nic.

items.en: I am perfectly happy here.
items.wrong: I am perfectly much happy here.
items.explanation: **perfectly** says nothing at all is missing.
items.explanation_cz: **perfectly** říká, že vůbec nic nechybí.

items.en: Dinner is almost ready.
items.wrong: Dinner is almost much ready.
items.explanation: **almost** = not quite there. A minute more and it is ready.
items.explanation_cz: **almost** = ještě to není. Ještě chvilku a je to.

items.en: We are nearly there.
items.wrong: We are nearly much there.
items.explanation: **nearly** and *almost* do the same job — close, but not arrived.
items.explanation_cz: **nearly** a *almost* dělají totéž — blízko, ale ještě ne u cíle.

items.en: The food was not particularly good.
items.cz: To jídlo nebylo nijak zvlášť dobré.
accepts: The food was not particularly good.
items.wrong: The food was not so much good.
items.explanation: **not particularly** is a polite way of saying not very. Never *not so much*.
items.explanation_cz: **not particularly** je zdvořilý způsob, jak říct not very. Nikdy *not so much*.

items.en: The film was so good.
items.wrong: The film was such good.
items.explanation: **so** goes straight in front of an adjective. *such* needs a noun after it.
items.explanation_cz: **so** stojí přímo před přídavným jménem. *such* za sebou potřebuje podstatné jméno.

items.en: It was so cold that we went home.
items.cz: Byla taková zima, že jsme šli domů.
items.gap: It was ____ cold that we went home. (so / such)
accepts: It was so cold that we went home.
items.wrong: It was such cold that we went home.
items.explanation: **so** + adjective + **that** + the result. The *that* half says what happened.
items.explanation_cz: **so** + přídavné jméno + **that** + následek. Část s *that* říká, co se stalo.

items.en: It was such a good film.
items.gap: It was ____ good film. (so / such a)
accepts: It was such a good film.
items.wrong: It was so a good film.
items.explanation: With a singular noun the phrase is **such a** + adjective + noun. *so a* is never English.
items.explanation_cz: U podstatného jména v jednotném čísle je vazba **such a** + přídavné jméno + podstatné jméno. *so a* v angličtině neexistuje.

items.en: They were such nice people.
items.wrong: They were so nice people.
items.explanation: A plural noun takes **such** with no *a*.
items.explanation_cz: Podstatné jméno v množném čísle má **such** bez *a*.

items.en: We had such bad weather.
items.wrong: We had so bad weather.
items.explanation: *weather* is uncountable, so it is **such** and no *a*.
items.explanation_cz: *weather* je nepočitatelné, takže **such** a žádné *a*.
